strategyDescription: Top-down: the full PR set is sent to a model that either declares it one coherent theme or splits it into two labeled parts along the strongest fault line. TypeScript validates every split is an exact partition of its input, then recurses on incoming parts (batches of 3, sets of <4 PRs stop, 34-call cap). Parts judged coherent become clusters; singletons become unclassified. Final partition, ranking and ids are validated in TypeScript.
noveltyRationale: Prior model strategies were bottom-up (per-PR facets, pairwise edges, chunk-local groups merged by a reduce). This one is top-down and adaptive: the model always sees the whole current set, makes binary split/stop judgments, and no chunking by PR number, pairwise edges, or closed vocabulary is used; membership is never merged across independently-formed groups.

lessonsForNextRun: Bash (node, python, sha256sum, lint, typecheck) was denied for the whole session; only view/create/grep/run_rig worked. Compute digests and independent validation need bash.
Stale files from earlier harness attempts (pr-clusters-result.json) block create; plan the output path to avoid collision.

Divisive bisection ran in only 9 calls and produced a dominant 23-PR cluster (55% of corpus); the 'coherent' stop criterion is lenient, so a broad CI/workflow bucket absorbs many distinct PRs. A depth or size-based forced split could add resolution.
No measured comparison against other strategies was made.
